newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks marginally lower in mid-week trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks marginally lower in mid-week trading.

text.p: Cyprus stocks showed signs of consolidation in mid-week trading on Wednesday, recording a loss of 0.23 points in the first three days of the week as opposed to 1.20 points in the first three trading days last week.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general share index closed at 82.99 on Wednesday, shedding 0.23 points from Friday's close of 83.22.
Floor brokers said half-yearly results expected from several large listed companies in the coming days may give the exchange a boost.

"I am not expecting significant changes unless we have such announcements by some public companies which will create further optimism," said Stavros Agrotis of CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
"A dividend policy might help the market but I think we need bigger events," he added.
The banking sub index closed at 89.89 points, steady over Friday's close of 89.85.

Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed higher at 342.5, adding 3.5 cents to Friday's close of 339. Fully paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 316.5, shedding 5.5 cents from 322 on Friday. The Cypriot-owned Hellenic Bank closed higher at 252.5, adding four cents from 248.5 on Friday.

Cyprus Airways, the island's state-controlled national carrier, fell to a year-low of 42.5 cents amid new tense labour relations between the pilots' union and management over the grounding of a pilot.

Last week airline chairman Vassilis Rologis submitted his resignation after his election as chairman of the Cyprus chamber of commerce and industry. He will remain at his post until a new appointment is announced by the government.

The share drop, below the nominal price of 50 cents, currently restricts the airline from proceeding with a rights issue. The rights issue is planned to reduce current government participation in the airline to 70 percent from 80 percent in line with stock exchange regulations.
Only 20 percent of the airline's capital is now traded on the exchange.
The sub index of insurance companies closed at 61.48 from 61.88 last week, while commercial companies gained 2.46 points to close at 69.41. ($=0.46 pounds)
